year_display.zh: 约公元前五至四世纪编成；1861 年英译

edition.en: Six of the twenty books, complete: I (Hsio R), II (Wei Chang), IV (Le Jin), VII (Shu R), IX (Tsze Han) and XV (Wei Ling Kung), from Legge’s The Chinese Classics, vol. 1 (1861; revised 1893), as transcribed on English Wikisource. The Chinese text Legge printed above each chapter is omitted here, since the original has its own place in the Open Stacks; paragraphs split by page breaks in the transcription are rejoined.
edition.zh: 二十篇中的六篇全文：学而、为政、里仁、述而、子罕、卫灵公，据英文维基文库所录理雅各《中国经典》第一卷（1861 年初版，1893 年修订）。理雅各在每章上方所印的中文原文这里不录，因为原典在开架书库另有位置；转录中被分页切断的段落已重新接合。

basis.en: An ancient Chinese text. James Legge, the translator, died in 1897; the translation was first published in 1861 and revised in 1893.
basis.zh: 中国先秦典籍。译者理雅各卒于 1897 年；译本 1861 年初版，1893 年修订。

note.en: Six books of the Analects in James Legge’s translation, chosen because between them they hold most of the sayings on learning, teaching and the passing of time: “at fifteen, I had my mind bent on learning”, “a transmitter and not a maker”, the river that does not cease day or night. Legge’s English is careful, Victorian and sometimes stiff; “the superior man” for junzi has been argued over ever since. Read it beside the Chinese original on the neighbouring shelf.
note.zh: 理雅各译《论语》六篇；选这几篇，是因为论学、论教、论时光流逝的话大多在其中：“吾十有五而志于学”，“述而不作”，“逝者如斯夫，不舍昼夜”。理雅各的英文审慎，带着维多利亚时代的气息，有时显得生硬；他把“君子”译作 the superior man，此后一直有人争论。请与旁边书架上的中文原典对照阅读。

excerpt.orig: The Master said, “If a man keeps cherishing his old knowledge, so as continually to be acquiring new, he may be a teacher of others.”
excerpt.en: The Master said, “If a man keeps cherishing his old knowledge, so as continually to be acquiring new, he may be a teacher of others.”
excerpt.zh: 子曰：温故而知新，可以为师矣。

note.en: Scored as a translation: Legge’s careful, learned version served English readers for generations, though its stiffness and choices such as ‘the superior man’ now feel dated.
note.zh: 按译本评分：理雅各的译文严谨博学，服务英文读者数代，但行文板滞，“君子”译作“superior man”已显陈旧。
